newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso falls to 27-mth low, recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso falls to 27-mth low, recovery seen.

text.p: The Philippine peso skidded to a 27-month low on Thursday but officials and dealers said the fall was temporary and did not reflect economic fundamentals.

The peso touched a low of 26.345 against the dollar in morning trade -- its lowest point since October 1994 -- on a sharp fall in domestic interest rates which was itself triggered by a cut last week in reserve requirements for banks.
Government officials said the peso's fall will be temporary since it was mostly due to speculation.
The peso started downward on Tuesday after the Philippine Central Bank slashed its overnight borrowing rate to 10.50 percent from 10.75 percent.

On Monday, the benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate plunged to 11.172 percent from 11.679 percent the previous week after an estimated 6.7 billion pesos were freed in banks by Friday's one percentage-point lowering of reserve requirements.
Dealers said the fall in rates had slashed interest rate differentials between the peso and the dollar, leading to a sell-off.

By 0840 GMT on Thursday, the peso had recovered marginally to 26.334 against the dollar, although it was still lower than Wednesday's 26.318. Volume was heavy at $335.30 million, more than double the daily normal volume of $150 million. The peso started the year at 26.286.
"We heard in the past two or three days that there was a lot of (dollar) buying because some banks servicing foreign investors here for the short-term have taken up their money.
"I think most of them have been serviced," said Cesar Zulueta, chief dealer of ING Bank.
"We were told investors' money is still here. There is no reason to shift to U.S. dollars," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters.
He said the peso still had a 3.5 percentage-point interest rate premium over the U.S. dollar.

Nevertheless, nervousness in the market increased when the Central Bank lifted its dollar selling rate to 26.345 early on Thursday from 26.33 in the previous session. Traders said it sent the wrong signal to the market.

"There was an outflow from offshore investors in the morning," Jaime Panganiban, country treasurer of Bank of America, told Reuters. But he said inflows and outflows balanced out over the past two days.

Another dealer said the peso could settle in the range of 26.30 to 26.34 since the Central Bank had been intervening to stabilise the market. The Central Bank said it sold slightly less than $15 million early on Thursday.
The Central Bank is well-armed to deal with any speculation with gross international reserves of $12.03 billion, analysts and traders said.
Another dealer said the peso could fluctuate in a wider range of 26.28 to 26.38 since there is a possibility of domestic interest rates falling another 0.50 of a percentage point.
Edeza said the Central Bank will take a wait-and-see approach on the peso speculation.
"We will have to re-assess as the situation arises," Edeza said. "This is partly speculative. There was also profit-taking on certain positions."
